subject: SLA addendum request: ramped uptime baseline and monthly credit schedule (Helios)
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@heliosretail.com>
To: mateo_alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@heliosretail.com
Date: 2026-09-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: SLA addendum for initial ramp (uptime and credits)

Hi Mateo / Laura —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are getting executive sign-off on the SOW but Legal has asked for an SLA addendum that accounts for the fact we'll be running a high-density batched inference pilot for 90 days. Specifically they want: 1) a temporary lower uptime baseline during the ramp window, and 2) a clear monthly credit schedule if availability or latency materially degrades.

Our asks:
- For the first 90 days post-launch, allow an agreed "ramp" baseline (we're proposing 99.5%) given load profiles;
- A simple monthly credit table tied to uptime buckets (we proposed a 10%/25% ladder depending on impact) and a cap equal to one month of service;
- A latency SLO (95th pctl) for inference for the production endpoints with credits if latency exceeds the threshold for more than 3 days in a month.

Attached is the redline Helios SOW that references the addendum sections we expect. Can Redwood propose language and the credit ladder so our legal team can review?

Appreciate a quick turnaround — we need to close procurement by Oct 6.

Best,
Elena
Director, Platform Engineering
Helios Retail

Attachments:
- Helios_SOW_v2.pdf (pdf)

From: mateo_alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@heliosretail.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-25T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA addendum for initial ramp (uptime and credits)

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the clear asks and for sharing the SOW. We can absolutely accommodate a short-term ramp baseline for the initial pilot window; below is a proposed starting point (we'll loop in Legal to finalize wording):

Proposed commercial terms (draft):
- Standard baseline after ramp: 99.90% monthly availability.
- Ramp window: first 90 days after production cutover: temporary baseline 99.70%.
- Monthly credit ladder (applies to invoice for the affected month):
  * Availability >= 99.70%: 0% credit
  * 99.50% <= Availability < 99.70%: 10% credit
  * 99.00% <= Availability < 99.50%: 25% credit
  * Availability < 99.00%: 50% credit (capped at 50% of that month's service charges)
- Latency SLO (inference 95th percentile): target < 200ms. If the 95th pctl exceeds 200ms for more than 3 calendar days in a month, we apply a 10% credit for that month (this stacks with availability credits but total monthly credit remains capped at 50%).
- Maintenance windows and agreed scheduled upgrades are excluded per the standard maintenance carveouts; we propose a max of four scheduled maintenance hours/month before credits apply.

I attached a short draft addendum to capture this language: SLA_Amendment_helios_draft.pdf. Two asks from our side to make monitoring/execution smoother:
1) Grant Redwood readonly access to the request trace IDs and a logging view for the endpoints so we can correlate incidents;
2) Confirm the expected monthly active token/embedding volume so we can size the reliability guards appropriately and avoid surprises.

If this looks reasonable I'll pull in Marissa (ops) and Laura (legal/account) to finalize.

— Mateo
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- SLA_Amendment_helios_draft.pdf (pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: mateo_alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-26T08:18:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: suggested tweaks to Mateo's draft credit ladder

Agree with the high level but want to propose operational tweaks before we send to the customer: 

- Suggested ramp baseline 99.65% (we've seen batched inference spikes push short-term availability dips); lowering to 99.65% reduces the chance of frequent credits while still giving Helios protection.
- Cap on scheduled maintenance carveouts: propose we limit scheduled maintenance to two 2-hour windows/month for the first 90 days (vs. four hours) but make them predictable (we publish windows in advance).
- Recommend the latency credit be measured per route group (search vs. generate endpoints) and triggered only if >1% of requests exceed 200ms on 3+ days — this avoids one-off noisy tails triggering credits.

If Aditya is ok commercially I can incorporate these into the addendum and track impact to projected MTTR and remediation runbooks.

— Marissa
Head of Reliability, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: SLA addendum for initial ramp (uptime and credits)

Elena —

Thanks for the patience while we reviewed internally. Helios's request is reasonable and we're prepared to offer a 90-day ramp with the following agreed terms (summary below and attached final addendum):

Final agreed summary (90-day ramp):
- Ramp baseline: 99.65% for the first 90 days after production cutover.
- Post-ramp baseline: 99.90% monthly availability.
- Monthly credit ladder (applies per affected invoice):
  * Availability >= 99.65%: 0% credit
  * 99.40% <= Availability < 99.65%: 10% credit
  * 99.00% <= Availability < 99.40%: 25% credit
  * Availability < 99.00%: 50% credit (cap 50% of that month's Redwood charges)
- Latency SLO: 95th pctl < 250ms for the ramp window (we'll tighten to 200ms post-ramp). Latency credits trigger only if >1% of requests exceed threshold on 3+ days in the month; credit size: 10% (stackable up to cap).
- Maintenance carveouts: two scheduled maintenance windows of up to 2 hours/month during ramp; emergency maintenance and customer-initiated changes are excluded.
- Monitoring/access: Redwood will be provided readonly request traces and aggregated logs for relevant endpoints (per the attached addendum).

Next steps: Laura (account/legal) to upload the addendum to DocuSign. Please review the attached Redwood_SLA_Addendum_vFinal.pdf and confirm acceptance by signing the DocuSign link below. Once signed and the production cutover date is set we'll start the 90-day clock.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/helios/df5b2a
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/HS-5583

If Helios Legal wants any narrow clarifying language we can address it quickly; otherwise we can proceed to signature.

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
Director, Strategic Accounts (Redwood Inference)
